units.function: HTTP integration tests for the custom API JSON compression middleware, including content negotiation, cache validators, streamed/download responses and Better Auth's writeHead plus Uint8Array response bridge.
units.dependencyDirection: Express routes emit responses through an API-scoped middleware that temporarily wraps ServerResponse write/end/flushHeaders, buffers eligible JSON and asynchronously applies node:zlib gzip or deflate before restoring the original methods.
units.keyDataModels: HTTP Accept-Encoding quality preferences, Content-Type/Encoding/Disposition/Range/Cache-Control, ETag and Content-MD5 validators, status/body eligibility, Buffer and Uint8Array chunks, write/end callbacks.
units.lifecycle: A request selects gzip or deflate before route execution. The middleware buffers JSON writes unless headers, streaming semantics or response metadata require passthrough; bodies below 1 KiB remain unchanged, eligible large bodies are compressed and validators adjusted, while compression failure falls back to the original bytes.
units.testAssessment: Ten real-socket tests strongly cover hot-list compression, both encodings, small/already-encoded/streamed/attachment responses, ETag weakening and the Better Auth Uint8Array regression. Missing are malformed and duplicate q-values, q=0 versus wildcard precedence, HEAD/204/304/errors, Cache-Control no-transform, flushHeaders, callback/backpressure ordering, client aborts, compression failure, Content-MD5 removal and a maximum buffered-body or concurrency memory bound.
units.designRationale: Reduce bandwidth on large JSON control-plane reads without corrupting authentication and download responses whose Node response semantics differ from ordinary res.json output.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS will return large task, evidence and office projections and needs transport efficiency that preserves identity cookies, evidence bytes, streaming and cache correctness under self-hosted and managed profiles.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the regression corpus and protocol guards, but prefer a maintained platform/proxy compression facility or a bounded implementation. Add Brotli where supported, hard buffer/concurrency limits, abort handling and metrics; never transform evidence downloads or signed/digested payloads unless the stored and transported representations are explicit.
units.responsibilityConflict: Compression is not a responsibility model, but silent byte transformation can invalidate evidence digests or obscure which representation was approved. The middleware buffers eligible JSON without an upper bound, creating a control-plane availability risk that is not exercised by the tests.

units.function: Unit tests for deterministic Vite HMR port selection and host advertisement when the server binds to concrete or wildcard interfaces.
units.dependencyDirection: Server startup configuration passes bind host and API port into pure helpers; their outputs configure Vite's middleware-mode HMR host, port and clientPort, without entering domain or persistence layers.
units.keyDataModels: TCP port range, privileged-port floor, wildcard IPv4/IPv6 bind host and concrete browser-reachable hostname.
units.lifecycle: Development startup chooses API port plus 10,000 when valid, otherwise subtracts 10,000 with a 1,024 floor. Wildcard bind hosts are omitted so the browser derives its hostname; concrete hosts are advertised unchanged.
units.testAssessment: Five concise pure-function cases cover upper-bound arithmetic, privileged/invalid avoidance and wildcard/concrete hosts. Missing are invalid/non-integer/negative server ports, actual port collision, IPv6 bracket/zone syntax, reverse-proxy/TLS HMR, hostile Host headers and end-to-end browser connectivity.
units.designRationale: Make the bundled development UI reachable from containers and LAN hosts while avoiding invalid HMR ports and incorrectly advertising 0.0.0.0 or :: to browsers.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs predictable local development and self-hosted UI tooling, but this is build-host plumbing rather than differentiated control-plane behavior.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Preserve the separation between bind address and browser-advertised address, but use the selected Web toolchain's supported configuration and collision detection rather than copying fixed-offset policy into Company OS core.
units.responsibilityConflict: None at the domain level. If development HMR is accidentally enabled on an exposed deployment, it expands the attack surface; profile validation must fail closed independently of this helper.

units.function: Truth-table tests for enabling the private-deployment hostname guard across local-trusted and authenticated deployment modes.
units.dependencyDirection: Deployment mode and exposure configuration flow into a pure enablement predicate; server composition then supplies the same allow-set to Express privateHostnameGuard and Vite allowedHosts before actor/auth routing.
units.keyDataModels: DeploymentMode local_trusted/authenticated, DeploymentExposure private/public, configured allowed hostnames, bind host and derived hostname allow-set.
units.lifecycle: At startup, both supported modes enable hostname validation only for private exposure. The resulting guard is installed before actor and authentication middleware, while Vite receives the allow-set in development mode; public exposure disables this private-host defense.
units.testAssessment: Four cases exhaust the current two-by-two predicate. They do not exercise the actual guard, Host/X-Forwarded-Host parsing, port/IPv6/IDNA normalization, DNS rebinding, proxy trust, empty/misconfigured allow-sets, public-mode safeguards or parity between Express and Vite enforcement.
units.designRationale: Defend private local deployments from browser Host-header and DNS-rebinding paths without imposing a private-host allowlist on deliberately public deployments.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS self-hosted/local enterprise deployments need an explicit exposure profile and DNS-rebinding defense that cannot be bypassed by choosing authenticated mode or by the development Web server.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the early host gate and shared allow-set concept. Make exposure/profile validation typed and fail-closed, test the real middleware behind representative proxies and IPv6, require explicit public-origin configuration, and keep Host validation additive to authentication, CSRF and origin controls.
units.responsibilityConflict: The predicate prevents one network confusion class but does not authorize a human or Agent. A public exposure flag disables it in both auth modes, so an operator mistake can remove the defense; the configuration change itself needs privileged audit and safe defaults.

units.function: Unit tests for deciding which development-mode GET requests receive the Vite-rendered single-page application shell instead of passing through to public assets or Vite source endpoints.
units.dependencyDirection: Express fallback routing calls a pure request classifier after API, auth, static and other server routes; accepted document requests reach the cached Vite HTML renderer, while known public/Vite paths call next().
units.keyDataModels: Express request path, Accept negotiation result, exact public static paths, Vite asset prefixes and SPA document route.
units.lifecycle: During vite-dev startup, public assets are mounted first and the catch-all GET route renders branded HTML only when the path is not reserved and negotiates HTML; otherwise downstream middleware handles or rejects it.
units.testAssessment: Three cases cover document routes, two public assets and two Vite prefixes. Missing are API/auth/plugin paths, HEAD/OPTIONS, encoded or traversal-like paths, query strings, case normalization, Accept quality combinations, missing assets, source maps, service-worker scope and an integration test proving route ordering cannot mask a 404/API error with HTML.
units.designRationale: Support client-side routing in development without returning index HTML for files and Vite module requests, which would create misleading MIME and caching failures.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a standalone Web development entry whose SPA fallback cannot intercept API, Connector, evidence or security endpoints and whose behavior matches production hosting.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Keep an explicit SPA fallback contract and production-parity integration tests, but derive exclusions from Company OS route ownership or place Web/API on clear boundaries instead of maintaining a fragile static prefix list.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct responsibility conflict. Incorrect fallback ordering could turn authorization or missing-resource responses into a successful HTML shell and hide control-plane failures from clients, so API namespaces and status semantics must remain unambiguous.
